en.title: 2-step garage
en.text: 2-step garage, or simply 2-step, is a genre of electronic music and a subgenre of UK garage. One of the primary characteristics of the 2-step sound – the term being coined to describe "a general rubric for all kinds of jittery, irregular rhythms that don't conform to garage's traditional four-on-the-floor pulse" – is that the rhythm lacks the kick drum pattern found in many other styles of electronic music with a regular four-on-the-floor beat.

en.title: Album-oriented rock
en.text: Album-oriented rock (AOR, originally album-oriented radio) is a radio format created in the United States in the late 1960s that focuses on the full repertoire of rock albums and is currently associated with classic rock. The format arose when American FM radio stations decided to play tracks by hard rock and progressive rock artists.

ja.title: アシッド・ハウス
ja.text: アシッド・ハウス（英: Acid house）は、ハウスミュージックのサブジャンル。1980年代半ばにアメリカ・シカゴで誕生し、ローランド製シンセサイザー「TB-303」を用いた独特なサウンドのベースラインを特徴としている。

en.title: Acid house
en.text: Acid house (also simply known as just "acid") is a subgenre of house music developed around the mid-1980s by DJs from Chicago. The style is defined primarily by the squelching sounds and basslines of the Roland TB-303 electronic bass synthesizer-sequencer, an innovation attributed to Chicago artists Phuture and Sleezy D circa 1986.

ja.title: アシッドジャズ
ja.text: アシッドジャズ（Acid jazz）は、1980年代にイギリス のクラブシーンから派生したジャズの文化。ジャズ・ファンクやソウル・ジャズ等の影響を受けた音楽のジャンル。

en.title: Acid jazz
en.text: Acid jazz (also known as club jazz, psychedelic jazz, or groove jazz) is a music genre that combines elements of funk, soul, and hip-hop. Acid jazz originated in clubs in London during the 1980s with the rare groove movement and spread to the United States, Western Europe, Latin America and Japan.

en.title: Acid rock
en.text: Acid rock is a loosely defined type of rock music that evolved out of the mid-1960s garage punk movement and helped launch the psychedelic subculture. While the term has sometimes been used interchangeably with "psychedelic rock", acid rock also specifically refers to a more musically intense, rawer, or heavier subgenre or sibling of psychedelic rock.

ja_tr.text: アシッド・ロックは、1960年代半ばのガレージ・パンクの流れから育ち、サイケデリックな若者文化の始まりを後押しした、輪郭のゆるいロックの一種。サイケデリック・ロックと同じ意味で使われることもあるが、より激しく、荒く、重いサイケデリック・ロックの一分野や、その兄弟のような音を特に指すこともある。

ja.title: オルタナティブR&B
ja.text: オルタナティブR&B（英: Alternative R&B）は、音楽評論家がオルタナティブスタイルのコンテンポラリー・R&Bを説明するために使用する用語。 90年代末にネオ・ソウルと呼ばれたR&B勢力の2000年代半ば以降の流れであり、音楽的には1990年代〜2000年代のR&Bからロックやクラシックまでもをサンプリングし、深いフィルターやエコーをかけたような音像と、トラップのような下地の効いたドラムを特徴とする。

en.title: Alternative R&B
en.text: Alternative R&B (also referred to as alt-R&B, indie R&B, and originally known as PBR&B, hipster R&B, emo R&B, or R-Neg-B) is a term used by music journalists to describe a stylistic alternative to contemporary R&B that began in the mid 2000s and came to prominence with musical artists such as Frank Ocean, Khalid, SZA, Summer Walker, Jhené Aiko, Brent Faiyaz, Zayn Malik, Tyler, the Creator, Steve Lacy, Childish Gambino, Miguel, Drake, The Weeknd, Kehlani, Tinashe, Bryson Tiller, PartyNextDoor, Tory Lanez, 6lack, and others. It is considered to be "more progressive and diverse" than its mainstream counterpart.

ja.title: オルタナティヴ・ロック
ja.text: オルタナティヴ・ロック（英語: Alternative rock）は、ロックのサブジャンル。主に1980年代半ばから1990年代半ばにかけてのポストパンク系バンドの総称であり、ジャングル・ポップ調の甘美なメロディからインダストリアル調の不穏で金属的な轟音までの幅広い音楽性が特徴。

en.title: Alternative rock
en.text: Alternative rock (also known as alternative music, alt-rock or simply alternative) is a category of rock music that evolved from the independent music underground of the 1970s. Alternative rock acts achieved mainstream success in the 1990s with the likes of the grunge subgenre in the United States, and the Britpop and shoegaze subgenres in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

ja_tr.text: オルタナティヴ・ロック（オルタナティヴ、オルタナとも）は、1970年代のインディーズやアンダーグラウンドの音楽から育ったロックの一分野。1990年代には、アメリカのグランジ、イギリスとアイルランドのブリットポップやシューゲイザーといった流れとともに、広く売れるようになった。

ja.title: 環境音楽
ja.text: 環境音楽（かんきょうおんがく、英: ambient music）、アンビエント・ミュージックは、伝統的な音楽の構成やリズムよりも音色や雰囲気を重視した音楽のジャンルである。正味の構成、ビート、構造化されたメロディを持たないこともある。

en.title: Ambient music
en.text: Ambient music is a genre of music that emphasizes tone and atmosphere over traditional musical structure or rhythm. Often "peaceful" sounding and lacking composition, beat, and/or structured melody, ambient music uses textural layers of sound that can reward both passive and active listening, and encourage a sense of calm or contemplation.

ja.text: アンビエント・テクノ（英: ambient techno）は、テクノの一ジャンル。アンビエント・ハウスと類似しているが、一般的なテクノで使用されるシンセサイザーやドラムマシンの音をより不明瞭にした音を特徴としている。

en.title: Ambient techno
en.text: Ambient techno is a subgenre of techno that incorporates the atmospheric textures of ambient music with the rhythmic elements and production of techno. It was pioneered by 1990s electronic artists such as Aphex Twin, Carl Craig, The Orb, The Future Sound of London, the Black Dog, Pete Namlook and Biosphere.

ja_tr.text: アンビエント・テクノは、アンビエントの空気のような響きに、テクノのリズムや音作りを合わせたテクノの一分野。Aphex Twin、Carl Craig、The Orb、The Future Sound of London、The Black Dog、Pete Namlook、Biosphereなど、1990年代の電子音楽の作り手が切り開いた。

ja.title: アート・ロック
ja.text: アート・ロック（Art rock）は、主に1960年代後半に登場した芸術的要素を持つロックバンドや、その作品を分類した音楽用語である。70年代初頭にはニュー・ロックという言葉も生まれている。

en.title: Art rock
en.text: Art rock is rock music that aims to distinguish the genre from popular entertainment, with the term typically being applied as the middle ground between mainstream and experimental rock. Art rock primarily draws influences from the wider art world and academia; which includes contemporary art, art music, avant-garde art, experimental music, avant-garde music, alongside classical music and jazz.

ja.title: バイレファンキ
ja.text: バイレファンキ（Baile Funk）は、1980年代に生まれたブラジル・リオデジャネイロのファベーラ発祥の音楽ジャンルの一つ。本場ブラジルではFunk Carioca（ファンキ・カリオカ）[ˈfɐ̃.ki ˌka.ɾi.ˈɔ.kɐ]などとも呼ばれる。

en.title: Funk carioca
en.text: Funk carioca (Brazilian Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfɐ̃k(i) kɐɾiˈɔkɐ, - kaɾ-]), also known as baile funk, Brazilian funk, or simply funk, is a Brazilian hip hop-influenced music genre from Rio de Janeiro, taking influences from musical styles such as Miami bass and freestyle. In Brazil, "baile funk" refers not to the music, but to the actual parties or discotheques in which the music is played (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈbajʎi], from baile, meaning "ball").

en.title: Baltimore club
en.text: Baltimore club, also called B'more club, B'more house or simply B'more, is a music genre that fuses breakbeat and house. It was created in Baltimore in the early 1990s by Frank Ski, Scottie B, Shawn Caesar, DJ Technics, DJ Class, DJ Patrick, Kenny B, among others.

ja.title: ベース・ミュージック
ja.text: ベース・ミュージック (Bass music) はクラブミュージックのジャンルの一つ。かつてはヒップホップのジャンルのひとつで、低音部を極端に強調したサウンドと速いBPMが特徴のマイアミ・ベースやアトランタ・ベースを指していた。

en.title: Bass music
en.text: Bass music is any of several genres of electronic dance music and hip hop music arising from the 1980s on, focusing on a prominent bass drum and/or bassline sound. As one source notes, there are "many different types of bass music to fall into, each putting a different spin on one of music's loudest elements".

en.title: Bassline (music genre)
en.text: Bassline (sometimes referred to as bassline house or 4x4 or niche) is a genre of electronic dance music that originated in South Yorkshire in the early 2000s. Stylistically it comprises a four-to-the-floor beat with a tempo of around 135–142 beats per minute and a heavy bass, similar to speed garage, with chopped up R&B and Pop vocal samples and a pop music aesthetic.

en.title: Bebop
en.text: Bebop or bop is a style of jazz developed in the early to mid-1940s in the United States. It is characterized by a fast tempo, complex chord progressions—with rapid chord changes, changes of key, angular melodies and substitute chords—along with virtuosic improvisation based on a combination of harmonic structure, scales, and occasional references to the melody.

Big bands originated during the early 1910s and dominated jazz in the early 1940s when swing was most popular.

en.text: Bitpop, also known as Chiptune Fusion, is a type of electronic music and subgenre of chiptune music, where at least part of the music is made using the sound chips of 8-bit (or 16-bit) computers and video game consoles.

en.title: Black metal
en.text: Black metal is an extreme subgenre of heavy metal music. Common traits include fast tempos, a shrieking vocal style, heavily distorted guitars played with tremolo picking, raw (lo-fi) recording, unconventional song structures, and an emphasis on atmosphere.

ja.title: ブルース
ja.text: ブルース（英語: blues、英語発音 [blú:z]）は、アメリカ合衆国深南部でアフリカ系アメリカ人の間から発生した音楽の一ジャンルである。19世紀後半ごろに米国深南部で黒人霊歌、フィールドハラー （農作業の際の叫び声）や、ワーク・ソング（労働歌）などから発展したものといわれている。

en.title: Blues
en.text: Blues is a music genre and musical form that originated among African Americans in the Deep South of the United States around the 1860s. Blues has incorporated spirituals, work songs, field hollers, shouts, chants, and rhymed simple narrative ballads from the African-American culture.

ja.title: ブルースロック
ja.text: ブルースロック (blues rock) は、ロック音楽のジャンルの一つ。1960年代以降のロックの中で、白人がブルースを、ロック的なスタイルで演奏したジャンルである。

en.title: Blues rock
en.text: Blues rock is a fusion genre and form of rock and blues music that relies on the chords/scales and instrumental improvisation of blues. It is mostly an electric ensemble-style music with instrumentation similar to electric blues and rock (electric guitar, electric bass guitar, drums, and sometimes with keyboards and harmonica).

ja.title: ブギウギ
ja.text: ブギウギ（boogie-woogie）は、ブルースのサブジャンルの一つであり、1920年代末頃に人気を博した。その原型はアフリカ系アメリカ人のコミュニティの中で1870年代頃から存在していたとされる。

en.title: Boogie-woogie
en.text: Boogie-woogie, also known as boogie, is a genre of blues music that became popular during the late 1920s, but had already developed in African-American communities since the 1870s. It was eventually extended from piano to piano duo and trio, guitar, big band, country and western, and gospel.

en.title: Breakbeat
en.text: Breakbeat is a broad type of electronic music that uses drum breaks, often sampled from early recordings of funk, jazz, and R&B. Breakbeats have been used in styles such as Florida breaks, hip-hop, jungle, drum and bass, big beat, breakbeat hardcore, and UK garage styles (including 2-step, breakstep and dubstep).

en.title: Breakbeat hardcore
en.text: Breakbeat hardcore (also referred to as hardcore rave, oldskool hardcore or simply hardcore) is a music genre that spawned from the UK rave scene during the early 1990s. It combines four-on-the-floor rhythms with breakbeats usually sampled from hip-hop.

ja_tr.text: ブレイクビート・ハードコア（ハードコア・レイヴ、オールドスクール・ハードコア、または単にハードコアとも）は、1990年代初めにイギリスのレイヴ・シーンから生まれた音楽ジャンル。四つ打ちのリズムに、ふつうはヒップホップからサンプリングしたブレイクビーツを組み合わせる。

ja.title: ブレイクコア
ja.text: ブレイクコア (英語: Breakcore) とは1990年代半ばから後半にかけて、ジャングル、ハードコア、ドラムンベースといったスタイルの中から現れたエレクトロニック・ダンス・ミュージックのスタイルの一つである。複雑で緻密なブレイクビートと幅広いサンプリング音源が高速なテンポで再生されることを特徴とする。

en.title: Breakcore
en.text: Breakcore is a style of electronic dance music that emerged from jungle, hardcore, and drum & bass in the mid-to-late 1990s. It is characterized by very complex and intricate breakbeats and a wide palette of sampling sources played at high tempos, though there is much debate in the breakcore subculture as to what breakcore itself is.

ja.title: ブリットポップ
ja.text: ブリットポップ（Britpop）またはブリットポップ・ムーブメント（Britpop Movement）は、1990年代にロンドンやマンチェスターを中心に発生したイギリスのポピュラー音楽ムーブメントである。ブリティッシュ・インヴェイジョン、グラム・ロック、パンク・ロックなど、イギリスのロック黄金期の影響を受けたバンドが多くデビューし、イギリス音楽界を盛り上げた。

en.text: Britpop was a British music and cultural movement that emerged in the 1990s. Musically, it produced bright, catchy alternative rock that drew heavily on the traditions of 1960s guitar-based British pop, with lyrics that emphasised national identity and offered commentary on British culture and society.

en.title: Broken beat
en.text: Broken beat (sometimes referred to as "bruk") is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in the late 1990s and is characterized by syncopated beats and frenetic, choppy rhythms, often alongside female vocals and elements inspired by 1970s jazz-funk. It has been heavily influenced by styles such as house, drum and bass, hip hop, techno, acid jazz, and R&B. The eclectic style generally avoided rigid four-on-the-floor rhythms and could make use of samplers, analogue synths, and live instrumentation.

ja_tr.text: ブロークン・ビート（「bruk」とも呼ばれる）は、1990年代末に現れたエレクトロニック・ダンス・ミュージック。拍をずらしたビートと、せわしなく途切れるリズムが特徴で、女性の歌声や、1970年代のジャズ・ファンクから来た要素を伴うことが多い。ハウス、ドラムンベース、ヒップホップ、テクノ、アシッド・ジャズ、R&Bなどの影響を強く受けている。決まった四つ打ちは避けられることが多く、サンプラー、アナログ・シンセ、生の楽器が使われる。

The style draws influences from trap, ambient and new age music to create a hazy, dreamlike, atmospheric and relaxed production style through the extensive use of reverb and ethereal chopped samples.

ja.title: コンテンポラリー・R&B
ja.text: コンテンポラリー・R&B（英: Contemporary R&B）は、リズム・アンド・ブルース、ソウル、ファンク、ヒップホップの要素を組み合わせ、ときにはドラムマシンなどの機器を使用した音楽ジャンルである。

en.title: Contemporary R&B
en.text: Contemporary R&B is a popular music genre, originating from African-American musicians in the 1970s that combines rhythm and blues with elements of pop, disco, funk, soul, jazz, blues, electronic and hip-hop. The incorporation of disco and electronic textures and production styles, which has come to prominence since the 2010s, brought forth a style called electro-R&B. The genre features a distinctive record production style and a smooth, lush style of vocal arrangement.

en.title: Cool jazz
en.text: Cool jazz is a style and genre of modern jazz music inspired by bebop and big band that arose in the United States after World War II. It is characterized by relaxed tempos and a lighter tone than that used in the fast and complex bebop style. Cool jazz often employs formal arrangements and incorporates elements of classical music.

en.title: Dangdut
en.text: Dangdut () is a genre of Indonesian folk music that is partly derived and fused from Hindustani, Arabic, and, to a lesser extent, Javanese, Malay, Minangkabau, Sundanese and local folk music. Dangdut is the most popular musical genre in Indonesia and very popular in other Maritime Southeast Asian countries because of its melodious instrumentation and vocals.

en.text: Electric blues is blues music distinguished by the use of electric amplification for musical instruments. The guitar was the first instrument to be popularly amplified and used by early pioneers T-Bone Walker in the late 1930s and John Lee Hooker and Muddy Waters in the 1940s.

en.title: Electro (music)
en.text: Electro (also known as electro-funk, and sometimes referred to as electro-pop) is a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the early 1980s. It is defined by the prominent use of the Roland TR-808 drum machine, and draws direct influence from early hip-hop and funk music.

en.text: Electroclash (also known as synthcore, retro-electro, tech-pop, nouveau disco) is a genre of popular music that fuses 1980s electro, new wave and synth-pop with 1990s techno, retro-style electropop and electronic dance music. It emerged in the late 1990s and was pioneered by and associated with acts such as I-F, DJ Hell, Miss Kittin and The Hacker, and Fischerspooner.

en.title: Garage rock
en.text: Garage rock (sometimes called garage punk or '60s punk) is a raw and energetic style of rock and roll that flourished in the mid-1960s, most commonly in the United States and Canada, and has experienced a series of subsequent revivals. The style is frequently characterized by basic chord structures played on electric guitars and other instruments, often distorted through a fuzzbox, as well as sometimes unsophisticated or aggressive lyrics and delivery.

en.title: Ghetto house
en.text: Ghetto house or booty house is a subgenre of house music which started being recognized as a distinct style from around 1992 onwards. It features minimal 808 and 909 drum machine-driven tracks and sometimes sexually explicit lyrics.

en.title: Glam rock

Glam artists drew on diverse sources, ranging from bubblegum pop and 1950s rock and roll to cabaret, science fiction, and complex art rock.

en.title: Glitch (music)
en.text: Glitch is a genre of experimental electronic music that emerged in the 1990s, distinguished by the deliberate use of glitches in audio media and other sonic artifacts. The genre takes its sounds from malfunctions in recording equipment and digital electronics, and its practitioners work from a philosophical position that treats errors and failures as compositional material rather than problems to be corrected.

en.title: Hyperpop
en.text: Hyperpop is an electronic music movement and loosely defined subgenre that originated in the early 2010s in the United Kingdom. It is characterised by an exaggerated or maximalist take on 21st century popular music tropes and typically integrates pop and avant-garde sensibilities while drawing on elements commonly found in electronic, rock, hip-hop, and dance music.

en.title: Intelligent dance music
en.text: Intelligent dance music (IDM) is a loose label used to describe experimental forms of electronic music associated with early-1990s ambient techno, "electronic listening music" and related forms of electronica. en.title: Illbient

The rhythm was rooted in hip hop over which repetitive phrases of jazz instrumentation, such as the trumpet, double bass, etc., were placed.

ja.text: クラウトロック（Krautrock）は、1960年代末から1970年代初めにかけて、西ドイツに登場した実験的（前衛的）ロックバンド群の音楽を指す、一般名詞である。

en.title: Krautrock
en.text: Krautrock (originally known as kosmische Musik, German for "cosmic music") is a broad genre of experimental rock that developed in West Germany in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Artists blend elements of psychedelic rock, avant-garde composition, and electronic music, among other eclectic sources.

en.text: Laptop twee is a style of twee pop that blends indie pop and indietronica with influences drawing from internet music and primarily DAW-based production. The genre emerged in the early 2020s, originally coined by the Canadian blogger and musician friends&.

en.title: Lo-fi hip hop
en.text: Lofi hip-hop (also known as chillhop) is a style of lo-fi music that combines hip-hop beats with elements of chill-out. The word lofi (also typeset as lo-fi, short for "low fidelity"), refers to the unpolished production techniques common in the style.

ja_tr.text: ローファイ・ヒップホップ（チルホップとも）は、ヒップホップのビートにチルアウトの要素を合わせたローファイ音楽のスタイル。ローファイ（lofi、lo-fiとも書き、「ロー・フィデリティ」を縮めた言葉）は、このスタイルによく見られる、磨きすぎない音作りのこと。

en.title: M-Base
en.text: The term "M-Base" is a term coined in the 1980s by American musician Steve Coleman to describe a new theory about creative expression. "M-Base-concept" is short for "macro-basic array of structured extemporization", and critics have used this term to categorize this scene's music as a style of jazz.

en.text: Miami bass (also known as booty music or booty bass) is a subgenre of hip-hop that became popular in the 1980s and 1990s. en.text: Minimal music (also called minimalism) is a form of art music or other compositional practice that employs limited or minimal musical materials. en.title: Modal jazz
en.text: Modal jazz is jazz that makes use of musical modes, often modulating among them to accompany the chords instead of relying on one tonal center used across the piece. Though exerting influence to the present, modal jazz was most popular in the 1950s and 1960s, as evidenced by the success of Miles Davis's 1958 composition "Milestones" and 1959 album Kind of Blue, and John Coltrane's quartet from 1960 to 1965.

ja.text: ネオ・ソウル（英: neo soul）は、1980年代末から1990年代にかけてアメリカ合衆国で形成された、コンテンポラリーR&Bおよびソウルミュージックの一形態。1970年代のソウル、ファンク、ゴスペル、ジャズの歌唱や演奏語法に、ヒップホップのビート、サンプリング、制作手法などを取り入れた音楽を指す。

en.title: Neo soul
en.text: Neo soul (sometimes called progressive soul) is a genre of popular music. As a term, it was coined by music industry entrepreneur Kedar Massenburg during the late 1990s to market and describe the style of music that emerged from soul and R&B. Evolving from soul music, neo soul is distinguished by a less conventional sound than its contemporary R&B counterpart, with elements ranging from funk, jazz fusion, hip-hop and rock.

en.title: Noise music
en.text: Noise music (or simply noise) is a subgenre of experimental music that is characterised by its use of unwanted noise as a primary musical element. The genre has roots in early 20th century avant-garde music, but later drew influence from industrial and electronic music.

ja.title: フォンク

en.title: Phonk
en.text: Phonk ( ) is a subgenre of hip hop that emerged in the early 2010s in the United States. The term was coined and popularized by American rapper and record producer SpaceGhostPurrp.

en.title: Power pop
en.text: Power pop is a subgenre of rock music and a form of pop rock based on the early music of bands such as the Beach Boys, the Beatles, the Byrds, and the Who. It typically incorporates melodic hooks, vocal harmonies, an energetic performance, and cheerful-sounding music underpinned by a sense of yearning, longing, despair, or self-empowerment.

en.title: Progressive metal
en.text: Progressive metal (often shortened to prog metal) is a broad fusion music genre melding heavy metal and progressive rock, combining the loud aggression and amplified distorted guitar-driven sound of the former with the more experimental, cerebral or quasi-classical compositions of the latter. The music typically showcases the extreme technical proficiency of the performers and usually uses unorthodox harmonies as well as complex rhythms with frequent meter changes and intense syncopation.

en.title: Ragtime
en.text: Ragtime, also spelled rag-time or rag time, is a musical style noted for its syncopated or "ragged" rhythm. It originated in African American communities in the late 19th century and was propelled to popularity in the 1890s to 1910s by composers such as James Scott, Joseph Lamb, and particularly Scott Joplin.

en.text: Rock music is a genre of popular music that originated in the United States as "rock and roll" in the late 1940s and early 1950s, developing into a range of styles from the late 1950s to mid-1960s, primarily in the United States and United Kingdom. en.title: Salsa music
en.text: Salsa is a style of dance music mainly influenced by Caribbean traditions and music from Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, and other countries such as Colombia and Venezuela, where African cultural syncretism in music and dance blends with European influences and indigenous instruments, along with contributions from the contiguous United States. en.title: Soft rock
en.text: Soft rock (also known as light rock, mellow rock or adult-oriented rock) is a form of rock music that originated in the late 1960s in the United States and the United Kingdom which smoothed over the edges of singer-songwriter and pop rock, relying on simple, melodic songs with big, lush productions. Soft rock was prevalent on the radio throughout the 1970s and eventually metamorphosed into a form of the synthesized music of adult contemporary in the 1980s.

ja.title: 霊歌
ja.text: 霊歌（れいか、スピリチュアルズ、英: Spirituals）は日本語では黒人霊歌（こくじんれいか）とも呼ばれ、アメリカ合衆国で誕生した宗教的な民謡 (英: folksong) の一つであり、奴隷状態に置かれていた南部のアフリカ系アメリカ人（黒人）の共同体の中から誕生した固有の宗教歌で、通常作者は不明である。これらの歌は18世紀後半の数十年間から1860年代に制度的奴隷制が廃止されるまでの間に黒人の共同体の中で育まれ、アメリカ民謡の最も幅広い重要な音楽形態の一つに発展した音楽。

en.title: Spirituals
en.text: Spirituals (also known as Negro spirituals, African American spirituals, Black spirituals, or spiritual music) is a genre of Christian music that is associated with African Americans, which merged varied African cultural influences with the experiences of being held in bondage in slavery, at first during the transatlantic slave trade and for centuries afterwards, through the domestic slave trade. Spirituals incorporate the "sing songs", work songs, and plantation songs that evolved into the blues and gospel songs in church.

ja.title: ヴェイパーウェイヴ
ja.text: ヴェイパーウェイヴ（またはベイパーウェーブ、蒸気波、英: Vaporwave）は、2010年代初頭にWeb上の音楽コミュニティから生まれた音楽のジャンルである。過去に大量生産されて忘れ去られた人工物や技術への郷愁、消費資本主義や大衆文化、1980年代のヤッピー文化、ニューエイジへの批評や風刺として特徴づけられる。

en.title: Vaporwave
en.text: Vaporwave is an internet music microgenre, aesthetic, and meme that emerged in the early 2010s. It is defined partly by its slowed-down, chopped and screwed samples of smooth jazz, elevator music, R&B, and lounge music from the 1980s and 1990s.

ja.title: ウエストコースト・ジャズ
ja.text: ウエストコースト・ジャズ（West Coast Jazz）は、1950年代、アメリカ合衆国ロサンゼルスを中心とする、アメリカ西海岸一帯で演奏されていたジャズの総称。ロックにもウエストコースト・ロックという地域ジャンルがある。

en.title: West Coast jazz
en.text: West Coast jazz refers to styles of jazz that developed in the American West Coast cities of Los Angeles and San Francisco during the 1950s. West Coast jazz is often seen as a subgenre of cool jazz, which consisted of a calmer style than bebop or hard bop.

ja.title: ゲームミュージック
ja.text: ゲームミュージックは、コンピュータゲームに付随する音楽のことである。ゲーム音楽、ビデオゲームミュージック（VGM）、ゲームBGMとも呼ばれている。

en.text: Video game music (VGM) is the soundtrack that accompanies video games. Early video game music was once limited to sounds of early sound chips, such as programmable sound generators (PSG) or FM synthesis chips.

ja.title: コンピュータ音楽
ja.text: コンピュータ音楽（コンピュータおんがく、computer music、コンピュータ・ミュージック）とは、コンピュータ技術の音楽の作曲や演奏への応用であり、作曲家が新しい楽曲を製作するサポートとしてコンピュータを利用したり、作曲アルゴリズムによりコンピュータが独自に楽曲を製作したりすることを指す。演奏への応用については、電子音楽との境界は曖昧である。

en.title: Computer music
en.text: Computer music is the application of computing technology in music composition, to help human composers create new music or to have computers independently create music, such as with algorithmic composition programs. It includes the theory and application of new and existing computer software technologies and basic aspects of music, such as sound synthesis, digital signal processing, sound design, sonic diffusion, acoustics, electrical engineering, and psychoacoustics.

ja.title: バロック音楽
ja.text: バロック音楽（バロックおんがく）は、ヨーロッパにおける17世紀初頭から18世紀半ばまでの音楽の総称である。この時代はルネサンス音楽と古典派音楽の間に位置する。

en.title: Baroque music
en.text: Baroque music (UK: or US: ) refers to the period or dominant style of Western classical music composed from about 1600 to 1750. The Baroque style followed the Renaissance period, and was followed in turn by the Classical period after a short transition (the galant style).

ja.text: ブラック・コンテンポラリー (Black Contemporary) は、ポピュラー音楽のジャンルの一つであるソウルの一種。日本ではブラコンと略して呼ばれることも多い。

en.title: Urban contemporary music
en.text: Urban contemporary music, also known as urban music, urban pop, or just simply urban, is a music radio format. The term was coined by New York radio DJ Frankie Crocker in the early to mid-1970s as a synonym for Black music.

ja.title: ルネサンス音楽
ja.text: ルネサンス音楽（ルネサンスおんがく）は、ヨーロッパにおいて、15世紀から16世紀のルネサンス期に作られた音楽の総称である。中世西洋音楽とバロック音楽の中間に位置し、その中心をなすのは、ポリフォニーによる声楽、とくに、宗教曲である。

en.title: Renaissance music
en.text: Renaissance music is traditionally understood to cover European music of the 15th and 16th centuries, later than the Renaissance era as it is understood in other disciplines. Rather than starting from the early 14th-century ars nova, the Trecento music was treated by musicology as a coda to medieval music and the new era dated from the rise of triadic harmony and the spread of the contenance angloise style from the British Isles to the Burgundian School.

ja.text: 十二音技法（じゅうにおんぎほう、英: Twelve-tone music、独: Zwölftonmusik）は、一般にはアルノルト・シェーンベルクが「五つのピアノ曲」作品23で1921年に完全に体系化した（とされる）作曲技法であり、ドデカフォニー（dodecaphony）や音列主義、セリエリズムなどとも呼ばれる。実際は「無調音楽」や「雑音音楽」「電子音楽」と同様に、同時代に複数の作曲家によって別々に独立して模索されてきた作曲技法である。

en.title: Twelve-tone technique
en.text: The twelve-tone technique—also known as dodecaphony, twelve-tone serialism, and (in British usage) twelve-note composition—is a method of musical composition. The technique is a means of ensuring that all 12 notes of the chromatic scale are sounded equally often in a piece of music while preventing the emphasis of any one note through the use of tone rows, orderings of the 12 pitch classes.

ja.title: 実験音楽
ja.text: 実験音楽（じっけんおんがく、英: experimental music）は、現代音楽のジャンル、潮流の一つである。音楽学においてはアメリカの作曲家、ジョン・ケージの導入した用語法として理解されている。

en.title: Experimental music
en.text: Experimental music is a general label for any music or music genre that pushes existing boundaries and genre definitions. en.title: Noh
en.text: Noh (能, Nō; Japanese pronunciation: [no(ꜜ)ː], Sino-Japanese for "ability") is a major form of classical Japanese dance-drama that has been performed since the 14th century. It is Japan's oldest major theater art that is still regularly performed today.

en.title: Art music
en.text: Art music (alternatively called classical music, cultivated music, serious music, and canonic music) is music considered to be of high phonoaesthetic value. It typically implies advanced structural and theoretical considerations or a written musical tradition.

ja_tr.text: 芸術音楽（クラシック音楽、教養音楽、シリアス・ミュージック、規範とされる音楽とも）は、音としての美的な価値が高いとされる音楽。ふつうは、高度な構造や理論への配慮、または楽譜に書かれた音楽の伝統を前提とする。

ja.title: 雅楽

en.title: Gagaku
en.text: Gagaku (雅楽, lit. "elegant music") is a type of Japanese classical music that was historically used for imperial court music and dances.

ja_own.text: Pure MIDIは、MIDI音源の内蔵エフェクトを切り、外のエフェクトもかけない素の音で作る音楽。ベロシティで音色の変わらないPCM音源のような響きが特徴で、実機のGM音源でもソフト音源でもよく、Windowsに入っているMSGSがいちばんよく使われる。ジャンルというより、決まりを決めて作る「縛り作曲」に近い。MLTEKや石引勲の音楽を元に、とぼけがおが名付けた。

en_own.text: Pure MIDI is music made with the raw sound of MIDI sound modules, with their built-in effects turned off and no outside effects added. It sounds like PCM tones that do not change with velocity; real GM modules and software instruments are both fine, and the MSGS synth built into Windows is the most used. It is closer to composing under a set of rules than to a genre. Tobokegao named it after the music of MLTEK and Isao Ishibiki.

ja_own.ref: NMPASS「#jesusclubって何？」（note）

en_own.text: #jesusclub is dance music built on Jersey club and similar styles, marked by a busy rhythm of seven kicks in a row. It is said to have begun as a "fictional genre" from a project by music fm and Abareflail; the hashtag came into use at the end of November 2024, and compilations followed in 2025.
en_own.ref: NMPASS, “What is #jesusclub?” (note, in Japanese)

ja_own.text: ゴルジェは、福岡出身のhanaliが2012年に始めた、タム（太鼓）を必ず使う音楽。登山や岩のイメージをまとい、「タムを使え、ゴルジェと呼べ、アートと呼ぶな」という決まりのもとで、誰でも参加して手を加えられる、オープンソースのようなジャンルとして広まった。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「A Guide to Gorge」

en_own.text: Gorge is music that always uses toms, started in 2012 by hanali from Fukuoka. Wrapped in images of mountain climbing and rock, it spread as an open-source-like genre that anyone can join and change, under the rule "Use toms. Call it Gorge. Don't call it art."
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, “A Guide to Gorge”

ja_own.text: ジャングルのなかの穏やかな流れで、ゆったりした和音や弦の音をブレイクビーツに重ねる。1990年代前半のロンドンで、LTJ BukemとレーベルGood Lookingのまわりから広まった。
ja_own.ref: The Vinyl Factory「An introduction to LTJ Bukem in 10 records」

en_own.text: A mellower strand of jungle that lays soft chords and strings over breakbeats. It grew in early-1990s London around LTJ Bukem and his Good Looking label.
en_own.ref: The Vinyl Factory, "An introduction to LTJ Bukem in 10 records" (Oli Warwick, 2018)

ja_own.text: 1991年にAphex TwinとGrant Wilson-Claridgeが始めたレーベルRephlexが、自分たちの型にはまらない音楽を呼ぶために作った名前。レーベルは、あらゆるジャンルのいちばんよいところを含むものと定めている。
ja_own.ref: Huck「Five things you didn't know about Aphex Twin」

en_own.text: A name coined by Rephlex, the label Aphex Twin and Grant Wilson-Claridge founded in 1991, for their hard-to-categorise output. The label defined it as the genre that takes in the best parts of every genre.
en_own.ref: Huck, "Five things you didn't know about Aphex Twin"

ja_own.text: ダブステップの低音を、中音域の荒く歪んだ音に移した派手なスタイル。2010年ごろ、RuskoのアルバムやSkrillexの「Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites」で広まった。
ja_own.ref: Dazed「What is brostep?」

en_own.text: A loud style of dubstep that moved the bass up into a harsh, distorted midrange. It took off around 2010 with Rusko's album and Skrillex's Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites.
en_own.ref: Dazed, "What is brostep?" (2024)

ja_own.text: 1920年代、ニューオーリンズからシカゴへ来た黒人の演奏家に学んだ、シカゴの若い白人たちが始めたジャズ。広い意味では、同じころシカゴで活動した黒人のジャズも含む。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「シカゴジャズ」（デジタル大辞泉）

en_own.text: Jazz started in 1920s Chicago by young white players who learned from Black musicians who had come up from New Orleans. In a wider sense it also covers Black jazz played in Chicago at the time.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "Chicago jazz" (Digital Daijisen)

ja_own.text: ダブステップの重さと攻撃性に、旋律と明るい響きを合わせたベースミュージック。2016年ごろ、イギリスのChimeが自分の音楽を呼ぶために作った名前で、レーベルRushdownの仲間に広まった。
ja_own.ref: Chime公式サイト「FAQ」

en_own.text: Bass music that pairs dubstep's weight and aggression with melody and bright harmony. Chime coined the name around 2016 for their own music, and it spread through the Rushdown label's artists.
en_own.ref: Chime's official site, FAQ

ja_own.text: Memphis Rapのドラムに、ブラックメタルから生まれたダンジョンシンセの音を重ねたヒップホップ。ロシア語圏のプロデューサーたちから始まり、DJ Sacredらが先駆けとされる。
ja_own.ref: Swampdiggers「DJ Naxxramasインタビュー」

en_own.text: Hip hop that puts Memphis rap drums under samples of dungeon synth, the fantasy-tinged offshoot of black metal. It began among Russian-speaking producers, with DJ Sacred among its pioneers.
en_own.ref: Swampdiggers, interview with DJ Naxxramas (2022)

ja_own.text: 1分間に1000拍を超えるほど速く、キックが拍ではなく音程のあるうなりに聞こえる、いちばん速いエレクトロニック・ミュージック。スピードコアから生まれ、1990年代末にベルギーのDJ Einrichが形を作ったとされる。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「An Introduction to Extratone」

en_own.text: The fastest electronic music, at 1,000 BPM or more, where the kicks blur into a pitched buzz rather than beats. It grew out of speedcore, and the Belgian DJ Einrich is credited with shaping it in the late 1990s.
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, "An Introduction to Extratone: The World's Fastest Music Genre" (Dave Jenkins, 2018)

ja_own.text: 主に1970年代のディスコやソウルのサンプルで作る、踊れるヴェイパーウェイヴの分かれ。快楽的で、未来より過去を懐かしむ。Saint Pepsi「Hit Vibes」（2013年）などが代表作。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree」

en_own.text: A danceable offshoot of vaporwave built mostly from 1970s disco and soul samples, hedonistic and looking back rather than forward. Saint Pepsi's Hit Vibes (2013) is a key record.
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, "Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree" (Simon Chandler, 2016)

ja_own.text: ポップスなどの曲を速めて音程を上げ、ブレイクビーツやJersey Clubのリズムに乗せる、せわしないマッシュアップ。2020年代はじめにJane Removerが始めたdariacoreの別名で、日本ではレーベルLost Frog Productionsを中心にこの名前で広まった。
ja_own.ref: Pitchfork「Remember Jane Remover's Mashup Genre Dariacore? It's Blowing Up in Japan Now」

en_own.text: Frantic mashup music that speeds up and pitches up pop songs and other samples over breakbeats and Jersey club rhythms. It is another name for dariacore, started by Jane Remover in the early 2020s, and spread in Japan under this name around the netlabel Lost Frog Productions.
en_own.ref: Pitchfork, "Remember Jane Remover's Mashup Genre Dariacore? It's Blowing Up in Japan Now" (Kieran Press-Reynolds, 2025)

ja_own.text: フューチャーベースの忙しい音に、ベルや木琴などのきらきらした音を重ねる、日本の「かわいい」エレクトロニック・ミュージック。Snail's House、Yunomi、YUC'eが代表とされ、かわいらしい雰囲気に反して重い低音や速いビートも多い。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「Eight Kawaii Artists Using Grotesque Sounds to Redefine 'Cute' Japanese Music」

en_own.text: Japanese "kawaii" electronic music that adds bells, xylophones and other sparkles to busy future bass. Snail's House, Yunomi and YUC'e are its best-known names, and despite the cute surface it often uses heavy drops and fast beats.
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, "Eight Kawaii Artists Using Grotesque Sounds to Redefine 'Cute' Japanese Music" (Patrick St. Michel, 2018)

ja_own.text: 1940年代、スウィングに行き詰まりを感じたCharlie ParkerやDizzy Gillespieらが、リズムや旋律、和音を新しくしたビバップから始まるジャズの総称。踊るための伴奏から、聴くための音楽へ変えた。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「モダンジャズ」（日本大百科全書、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典）

en_own.text: The umbrella name for jazz from 1940s bebop onward, when Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie and others reworked rhythm, melody and harmony after swing had grown stale. It turned jazz from dance accompaniment into music for listening.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "Modern jazz" (Nipponica; Britannica Japan concise)

ja_own.text: 20世紀初めから1920年代にかけて、ニューオーリンズのクレオールや黒人の演奏家が生んだ、いちばん早い時期のジャズ。ブラスバンドがもとで、何人もが同時に即興で旋律を重ねる合奏が特徴とされる。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「ニューオーリンズ・ジャズ」（ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典）、ブリタニカ「New Orleans style」

en_own.text: The earliest style of jazz, played by Creole and Black musicians in New Orleans from the early 1900s into the 1920s. It grew from brass bands and is known for collective improvisation, with several players varying the melody at once.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "New Orleans jazz" (Britannica Japan concise); Encyclopaedia Britannica, "New Orleans style"

ja_own.text: 1940年代にStan Kentonが掲げた呼び名で、即興よりも凝った編曲と、大胆な金管の響きを前に出したビッグバンドのジャズ。広くモダンジャズ全体を指して使われることもある。
ja_own.ref: ブリタニカ「Stan Kenton」「progressive jazz」

en_own.text: A label Stan Kenton attached to his band's music in the 1940s, putting elaborate arrangements and bold brass voicings ahead of improvisation. Some also use it loosely for modern jazz in general.
en_own.ref: Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Stan Kenton" and "progressive jazz"

ja_own.text: 低音のくり返しを中心にした、飾りの少ないダブステップ。2012〜2013年ごろのSubfiltronikらの曲が型とされ、早いころのダブステップの暗さを引き継いでいる。
ja_own.ref: UKF「Infekt's Guide To Riddim」

en_own.text: A stripped-back dubstep built on repetitive bass loops. Tracks made around 2012–2013 by Subfiltronik and others are seen as its blueprint, carrying on the darkness of early dubstep.
en_own.ref: UKF, "Infekt's Guide To Riddim" (Dave Jenkins)

ja_own.text: ドイツのフランクフルトで生まれた、歪んで暗く硬いテクノ。DJのChris Liebingが自分のかける音を呼ぶために作った言葉で、ドイツ語としての意味はないと本人が語っている。
ja_own.ref: The Music「Chris Liebing」インタビュー

en_own.text: Dark, distorted, hard techno from Frankfurt, Germany. DJ Chris Liebing made up the word for the music he played, and says it has no real meaning in German.
en_own.ref: The Music, interview with Chris Liebing

ja_own.text: 古いラジオやテレビの断片を、チャンネルを次々に変えるように切り貼りする、ヴェイパーウェイヴのいちばん生の形。「broken transmission」とも呼ばれる。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree」

en_own.text: The rawest form of vaporwave, collaging forgotten radio and TV clips as if flipping through channels. It is also called "broken transmission".
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, "Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree" (Simon Chandler, 2016)

ja_own.text: ヴェイパーウェイヴのなかで、とても澄んだ音が特徴のスタイル。Windows 95やSkypeの起動音など、ひと昔前のコンピューターや商業の音を使い、2011年のJames Ferraro「Far Side Virtual」から生まれた。
ja_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily「Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree」

en_own.text: A strand of vaporwave marked by an almost squeaky-clean sound, using the start-up chimes of Windows 95, Skype and other sounds from the not-too-distant past of computing and commerce. It was born with James Ferraro's Far Side Virtual in 2011.
en_own.ref: Bandcamp Daily, "Genre As Method: The Vaporwave Family Tree" (Simon Chandler, 2016)

ja_own.text: 1990年代の渋谷系の響きを引き継ぐ、21世紀の日本のポップの流れ。ネット動画の広がりとともに、Perfumeやきゃりーぱみゅぱみゅのような世界的なヒットを生んだ。
ja_own.ref: 現代ビジネス、難波功士「オリンピック、きゃりーぱみゅぱみゅにも影響した、90年代「渋谷系」音楽の遺産」

en_own.text: A 21st-century current in Japanese pop that carries the echo of 1990s Shibuya-kei. Alongside the spread of online video it produced global stars such as Perfume and Kyary Pamyu Pamyu.
en_own.ref: Gendai Business, Koji Namba (Kwansei Gakuin University), on the legacy of 1990s Shibuya-kei (2021)

ja_own.text: 歌詞と旋律を入れると歌声を合成するソフト、VOCALOIDを使って作る歌。ヤマハが2003年に技術を作り、2007年の「初音ミク」で広く知られた。作り手が曲を動画サイトに出し、聴き手が絵や映像を付けて出し直す、共同の作り方が育った。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「ボーカロイド」（デジタル大辞泉、日本大百科全書）

en_own.text: Songs made with VOCALOID, software that synthesizes a singing voice from lyrics and melody. Yamaha developed it in 2003, and it became widely known with Hatsune Miku in 2007. A collaborative culture grew up around it, with creators posting songs to video platforms and listeners adding artwork and videos.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "Vocaloid" (Digital Daijisen; Nipponica)

ja_own.text: 神楽、東遊、久米舞など、大陸の音楽が来る前から日本にあった歌と舞。大陸の楽舞が入ってきたのをきっかけに、宮廷の雅楽寮で教えられる芸として整えられた。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「雅楽」（改訂新版 世界大百科事典、日本大百科全書）

en_own.text: Japan's own songs and dances, such as kagura, azuma-asobi and kume-mai, that predate music from the continent. The arrival of continental music and dance led the court's music bureau to organise and teach them.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "Gagaku" (Heibonsha World Encyclopedia; Nipponica)

ja_own.text: 雅楽のうち、舞を伴わずに楽器だけで演奏する合奏。笙・篳篥・笛の管と、箏・琵琶の絃、羯鼓などの打楽器で演奏する。平安時代、貴族の音楽の集まり「御遊」から生まれた。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「管絃」（改訂新版 世界大百科事典、日本大百科全書）

en_own.text: The purely instrumental side of gagaku, played without dance. Winds (shō, hichiriki, flute), strings (koto, biwa) and percussion such as the kakko play together. It grew out of Heian aristocrats' music gatherings called gyoyū.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "Kangen" (Heibonsha World Encyclopedia; Nipponica)

ja_own.text: 1990年代のMemphis Rapの流れをくむphonkから生まれ、ロシアのプロデューサーたちが広めたスタイル。不気味なリズムと音程をずらした旋律が特徴で、ドリフト走行の動画とともにTikTokで広まった。
ja_own.ref: サンシャイン・コースト大学（The Conversationより転載）「How a global crisis, drift racing and Memphis hip-hop gave us phonk」

en_own.text: A style of phonk, itself rooted in 1990s Memphis rap, championed by Russian producers. Known for ominous rhythms and detuned melodies, it spread on TikTok paired with videos of drift racing.
en_own.ref: University of the Sunshine Coast / The Conversation, "How a global crisis, drift racing and Memphis hip-hop gave us phonk" (Ward, Luttrell, Goold, 2024)

ja_own.text: スピードコアのなかでも最も実験的な領域にある、ダンスを目的としない電子音楽。フランスのLa Peste（Laurent Mialon）が名付けた言葉で、彼のレーベルHangars Liquidesでは、2001年ごろから4つ打ちのキックをばらし、短いノイズや電子音響の響きで組み立てた曲が中心になった。
ja_own.ref: Spannered、Jon Weinel「Flashcore: Earth, Atomizer, Let's Go!」（2007年、Web Archive）

en_own.text: Non-danceable electronic music at the far experimental edges of speedcore. Coined by French artist La Peste (Laurent Mialon), the term came to define the sound of his label Hangars Liquides around 2001, deconstructing the four-on-the-floor kick into brief bursts of noise and electroacoustic textures.
en_own.ref: Jon Weinel, "Flashcore: Earth, Atomizer, Let's Go!", Spannered (2007, via Web Archive)

ja_own.text: 1990年代半ばのイギリスで、プログレッシブ・ハウスの流れとともに育ったトランス。SashaやJohn Digweedらがブレイクビーツやハウス、テクノの要素を取り入れ、長くうねるように感情を高めるDJセットを生み出しました。初期を支えたレーベルには、1992年設立のPlatipusやHooj Choonsなどがあります。
ja_own.ref: Beatportal「Beatport's Definitive History of Trance」（Arjan Rietveld、2021年）

en_own.text: Trance that grew in mid-1990s Britain alongside progressive house. DJs like Sasha and John Digweed incorporated breakbeat, house, and techno to craft long, hypnotic, emotional sets, with Platipus (founded in 1992) and Hooj Choons serving as early cornerstones.
en_own.ref: Beatportal, "Beatport's Definitive History of Trance" (Arjan Rietveld, 2021)

ja_own.text: フットワーク（ジューク）に、ブレイクコアやハードコアを掛け合わせた音楽。2019年4月、Dochakuso Recordsが19曲入りのコンピレーション『FOOTCORE COMPILATION』でこの名前を掲げ、「やりすぎたFootwork Jungle」と紹介した。2020年には24曲入りの第2弾も発表された。
ja_own.ref: Dochakuso Records「[DCKS-0084] V.A. - FOOTCORE COMPILATION」

en_own.text: Music that crosses footwork (juke) with breakcore and hardcore. In April 2019, Dochakuso Records introduced the term with the 19-track compilation FOOTCORE COMPILATION, describing it as "Footwork Jungle gone too far"; a second, 24-track volume followed in 2020.
en_own.ref: Dochakuso Records, "[DCKS-0084] V.A. - FOOTCORE COMPILATION"

ja_own.text: GAMEBOYなどのゲーム機の音で作るチップチューンの流れの一つ。イギリスのSabrepulseが先駆けの一人で、2006年1月にアルバム『Chipbreak Wars』を出した。
ja_own.ref: Sabrepulse本人のBandcamp（プロフィールと『Chipbreak Wars』のページ）

en_own.text: A strand of chipmusic made with game hardware, most notably the Game Boy. Brighton's Sabrepulse was one of its pioneers; his album Chipbreak Wars came out in January 2006 on Give Daddy The Knife / Merryworks Japan.
en_own.ref: Sabrepulse's own Bandcamp (artist bio and the Chipbreak Wars page)

ja_own.text: イギリス・ブリストルのbye2が自分の音楽につけた呼び名で、ジャングルやブレイクコアに近い音。2020年のアルバム『Ghost Worm』の舞台「Orb Universe」と同じ「Orb」を使い、本人は型にしばられない「なんでもあり」の言葉だと話している。
ja_own.ref: ETHEREAL.PRESSのbye2インタビュー（Internet Archiveの2024年の保存）

en_own.text: The name Bristol producer bye2 gives to their own music, which is often compared to jungle and breakcore. It shares the 'Orb' of the Orb Universe, the imaginary setting of bye2's 2020 album Ghost Worm, and bye2 calls it a junk term that means anything goes.
en_own.ref: "Bye2 - Interview", ETHEREAL.PRESS (archived April 2024)

ja_own.text: フォンクの流れの一つで、フロリダの影響を受けた、すっきりしたトラップに近い音。トラックの音に埋もれずラップの声がはっきり前に出て聞こえるのが特徴で、YouTubeでメンフィス・ラップを紹介するRyan Celsiusがこう呼んでいる。
ja_own.ref: Rolling Stone「Russian Producers Obsessed With Three 6 Mafia Can't Stop Going Viral」（Elias Leight、2021年4月29日）

en_own.text: A strand of phonk with Florida roots and a cleaner, almost mainstream trap sound, where the rapper's voice stays clear on top of the mix. The term was coined by Memphis-rap YouTube curator Ryan Celsius, as reported by Rolling Stone in 2021.
en_own.ref: Elias Leight, "Russian Producers Obsessed With Three 6 Mafia Can't Stop Going Viral", Rolling Stone, 29 April 2021

ja_own.text: sewerslvtが自分の曲につけたジャンル名。深くリバーブをかけたシンセの響きのなか、アーメンブレイクをあまり刻まずに鳴らし続ける、鬱々としたブレイクコアを指す。「Draining Love Story」の人気をきっかけにTikTokやSpotifyで広まり、似た作風の作り手が大勢現れた。
ja_own.ref: しぎ「異端児sewerslvtと彼女が残した功罪（4）（終）」（note）

en_own.text: A genre name coined by sewerslvt for this sound: gloomy breakcore featuring heavily reverbed synth pads and a continuously running, barely chopped Amen break. Following the breakthrough of "Draining Love Story," the style spread across TikTok and Spotify, inspiring many other producers.
en_own.ref: Shigi, "異端児sewerslvtと彼女が残した功罪（4）（終）" (note, in Japanese)

ja_own.text: 流行歌を切れ目なくつないで歌い、かけ声や合いの手を重ねていく、韓国の大衆音楽。観光バスのガイドだった李博士（イ・パクサ）が1989年のカセット『シンパラム李博士 1集』で人気を集め、1996年には日本でもアルバムが出た。
ja_own.ref: BRUTUS「韓国文化通信 Vol.15 ポンチャック歌手・Lee Park Sa」

en_own.text: A style of Korean popular music that strings together well-known songs into nonstop medleys, topped with shouts and ad-libs. Lee Park-sa, a former tour-bus guide, had a hit with his 1989 cassette Shinparam Ipaksa 1 and released albums in Japan in 1996.
en_own.ref: BRUTUS, "Korean Cultural News Vol. 15: Ponchak Singer Lee Park Sa"

ja_own.text: 1990年代はじめに生まれた、速く荒々しいテクノ。Jeff Millsが1992年にベルリンのTresorから出した『Waveform Transmission Vol. 1』の、当時としては速いループの音が、その流れの始まりとされる。
ja_own.ref: Ben Cardew「How Jeff Mills' 'Waveform Vol. 1' started a new era of techno」DJ Mag（2022）

en_own.text: A faster, harsher strain of techno that took shape in the early 1990s. Jeff Mills's 1992 album "Waveform Transmission Vol. 1" on Berlin's Tresor, built on relentless loops at up to 149 bpm, is credited with starting it.
en_own.ref: Ben Cardew, "How Jeff Mills' 'Waveform Vol. 1' started a new era of techno", DJ Mag (2022)

ja_own.text: 2013年にロンドンでA. G. Cookが始めたレーベルPC Musicのまわりで生まれた電子ポップ。ユーロダンスの派手なシンセ、グライムの低音、ハッピーハードコアの高い声に、わざとかわいらしさを強調した表現を合わせた音楽で、のちのハイパーポップの最初の波とされる。
ja_own.ref: Kieran Press-Reynolds「The Lost Promises of Hyperpoptimism」Pitchfork（2024）、Lanre Bakare「PC Music: clubland's cute new direction」The Guardian（2014）

en_own.text: Electronic pop from the circle around PC Music, the London label A. G. Cook started in 2013, pairing Eurodance-style synths, grime sub-bass and pitched-up happy-hardcore vocals with a deliberately cute image. It is considered the first wave of what became hyperpop.
en_own.ref: Kieran Press-Reynolds, "The Lost Promises of Hyperpoptimism", Pitchfork (2024); Lanre Bakare, "PC Music: clubland's cute new direction", The Guardian (2014)

ja_own.text: ロックに根をもつバンドが、シンセサイザーやサンプラー、ドラムマシンを使って作る音楽をまとめた呼び名。1990年代はじめのStereolabやDisco Infernoが最初の波で、2000年代に宅録とソフトシンセが広まって一気に増えた。
ja_own.ref: AllMusic「Indie Electronic」

en_own.text: A catch-all for rock-rooted acts making music with synthesizers, samplers and drum machines, drawing on krautrock, synth-pop and early electronic composers. The first wave came in the early 1990s with Stereolab and Disco Inferno, and it grew fast in the 2000s as home recording spread.
en_own.ref: AllMusic, "Indie Electronic"

ja_own.text: 南アフリカで、おもにツォンガ語で歌われるディスコ。1985年にPaul Ndlovuが最初の曲を出したのが始まりで、のちにJoe Shirimaniが自作やPenny Pennyのプロデュースで受け継いだ。
ja_own.ref: Ignatia Madalane「From Paul to Penny: the emergence and development of Tsonga disco 1985-1990s」African Music 10(1)（2015）

en_own.text: Disco from South Africa sung mainly in Xitsonga. It began with Paul Ndlovu's first songs in 1985 and was carried on by Joe Shirimani, both in his own records and as writer-producer for Penny Penny.
en_own.ref: Ignatia Madalane, "From Paul to Penny: the emergence and development of Tsonga disco 1985-1990s", African Music 10(1) (2015)

ja_own.text: 1970年代前半から出てきた日本のポピュラー音楽。フォークやロックの影響を受けた歌い手が自分で曲を作って歌い、それまでの歌謡曲と違って、アルバムとコンサートを中心に支持を集めた。
ja_own.ref: コトバンク「ニューミュージック」（百科事典マイペディア、デジタル大辞泉、精選版 日本国語大辞典）

en_own.text: Japanese popular music that emerged in the early 1970s, made mostly by singer-songwriters influenced by folk and rock. Unlike kayōkyoku, it won its audience mainly through albums and concerts rather than the media-driven hit system.
en_own.ref: Kotobank, "New Music" (Hyakka Jiten Mypedia; Digital Daijisen; Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten)

ja_own.text: Ambient Pluggからさらに派生したラップ。浮遊感のあるシンセの音、変則的なドラム、気だるくつぶやくような歌い方、皮肉でダークな歌詞が特徴で、2026年にSIE Collectiveのkllhhrの「skin」がバイラルヒットして注目が集まった。
ja_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由「2026年注目度急上昇サブジャンルAMBIENT RAPについて知ってること」note（2026）

en_own.text: A further offshoot of ambient plugg, with floating synths, irregular hi-hats, a languid, mumbled flow and ironic, dark lyrics. It drew wide attention in 2026 after "skin" by kllhhr of SIE Collective went viral.
en_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由 (hotmilkissweet), "2026年注目度急上昇サブジャンルAMBIENT RAPについて知ってること", note (2026)

ja_own.text: Pluggから派生したサブジャンル。Izaya Tiji、Duwap Kaine、SummrsらSlayworld周辺のアーティストが源流として語られることが多く、990xや.cutspaceなどクリック＆カット系の電子音楽の作り手と合流して、一つのジャンルになった。
ja_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由「2026年注目度急上昇サブジャンルAMBIENT RAPについて知ってること」note（2026）

en_own.text: An offshoot of plugg. Its roots are usually traced to Izaya Tiji, Duwap Kaine, Summrs and others around Slayworld, and it settled into a genre of its own when it met click-and-cut electronic producers such as 990x and .cutspace.
en_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由 (hotmilkissweet), "2026年注目度急上昇サブジャンルAMBIENT RAPについて知ってること", note (2026)

ja_own.text: アトランタのプロデューサーMexikoDroが、StoopidXoolと2013年に作った集団BeatPluggzから始まったトラップの一種。Zaytovenの影響を受けた激しい重低音（808）と、くり返し耳に残るメロディーで、SoundCloudを通して広まった。
ja_own.ref: SoundCloud Stories「Dive into Atlanta’s underground Hip-Hop community in SCENES: plugg」

en_own.text: A style of trap that began in Atlanta with BeatPluggz, the collective that producer MexikoDro formed with StoopidXool in 2013. Its aggressive 808s and hypnotic melodies, drawn from Zaytoven's production, spread quickly across SoundCloud.
en_own.ref: SoundCloud Stories, "Dive into Atlanta’s underground Hip-Hop community in SCENES: plugg"

ja_own.text: Pluggから分かれた暗い作風。地を揺らすような重低音（808）とゆがんだメロディーが特徴で、tdf、boolymon、perc40らのプロデューサーが形を作ってきた。
ja_own.ref: Vivian Medithi「Goxan on Lazer Dim 700, dark plugg, and alarm 808s」The FADER（2025）

en_own.text: A darker offshoot of plugg, built on enormous 808s and warped melodies, defined and refined by producers such as tdf, boolymon and perc40.
en_own.ref: Vivian Medithi, "Goxan on Lazer Dim 700, dark plugg, and alarm 808s", The FADER (2025)

ja_own.text: ivvys、maajins、sxpranoの3人のプロデューサー集団#stepTeamから生まれた作風で、つまずいて跳ねるように聞こえる変則的なドラムが特徴。リズムの元として、ivvysはアンビエントなトラップ、EDM、フットワークを挙げている。
ja_own.ref: Vivian Medithi「How ivvys and #stepTeam unlocked new rhythms in rap production」The FADER（2025）

en_own.text: The style of #stepTeam, the producer trio of ivvys, maajins and sxprano, built on syncopated drums that seem to skip, stutter and glitch. ivvys names ambient trap, EDM and footwork as the sources of its rhythms.
en_own.ref: Vivian Medithi, "How ivvys and #stepTeam unlocked new rhythms in rap production", The FADER (2025)

ja_own.text: 決まった音ではなく、作り方の姿勢を指すヒップホップの呼び名。ドリルやブーンバップのようにドラムで聞き分けられるものではなく、大手レーベルのふつうのラップの枠から外れたものが、広く「エクスペリメンタル」と呼ばれてきた。
ja_own.ref: andre gee「So What Exactly is Experimental Rap Anyway? We Asked Six Rappers, Producers and Journalists」Okayplayer（2026）

en_own.text: A label for hip hop that names an approach rather than a sound. Unlike drill or boom bap, it cannot be identified by its drums alone, and almost anything that steps outside the confines of a conventional major-label rap release has been called experimental.
en_own.ref: andre gee, "So What Exactly is Experimental Rap Anyway? We Asked Six Rappers, Producers and Journalists", Okayplayer (2026)

ja_own.text: HexDから派生したダンスミュージック。Hyperpopの影響が強く、あえて音質を粗く荒らした（ビットクラッシュした）音が多い。2022年の終わりごろにLumi Athenaの「Smoke It Off!」がTikTokで広まり、似た曲がたくさん作られた。
ja_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由「2023年の覇権ジャンル、Krush Club(HexD),Sigilkoreについて」note（2023）

en_own.text: A dance offshoot of HexD with a strong hyperpop influence, usually (though not always) bitcrushed. After Lumi Athena's "Smoke It Off!" spread on TikTok around the end of 2022, a wave of similar tracks followed.
en_own.ref: ホットミルクが甘い理由 (hotmilkissweet), "2023年の覇権ジャンル、Krush Club(HexD),Sigilkoreについて", note (2023)

ja_own.text: インドネシアのリミックス音楽を中心に、速く、力強いビートと重低音のEDMを指す言葉。名前は、ビートの「ドゥッ、ドゥッ」という音から来ている。SNSの利用者が、ダンドゥットを混ぜてリミックスしたEDMを呼ぶのに使い始め、コロナ禍のTikTokで広まった。ビートに合わせて写真や映像がテンポよく切り替わる動画編集とセットで親しまれている。
ja_own.ref: Wendy Belinda Tiantini、Nadya Afdholy、Yulia Mega Puspita「Jamet Stereotyping in Jedag-Jedug Music」Jurnal Seni Musik（2023）

en_own.text: A term for fast, bass-heavy EDM, especially Indonesian remix music. The name is an onomatopoeia for the beat ("dug, dug"). Social media users began using it for EDM remixed with dangdut, and it spread on TikTok during the pandemic, closely tied to video edits that flash photos and clips in sync with the beat.
en_own.ref: Wendy Belinda Tiantini, Nadya Afdholy and Yulia Mega Puspita, "Jamet Stereotyping in Jedag-Jedug Music", Jurnal Seni Musik (2023)
